raised_by: todo-metadata-layer roadmap's resolver-coverage work: 57 -> 111 (+54). Two mechanisms landed together and are both proved by corpus_resolution_snapshot.py at 0 lost / 0 moved: (1) resolve_symbol()'s head search is no longer capped at 512 lines (_DEF_HEAD_LIMIT removed, bounded instead by _MAX_FILE_BYTES on the input) -- +35 refs whose single-line definitions sat past the old cap, e.g. kmalloc at src/kernel/mm/heap.c:666 and schedule at src/kernel/sched/task.c:1721; (2) a new follow_declaration() follows a header-only ref to its repo-convention sibling .c (include/ mirrors src/, CLAUDE.md 'Repository Layout') when the header carries only a forward declaration -- +18/20 of the corpus's decl-only population (basename-unique, non-static; the 2 non-header extern-in-.c cases stay unresolved, not guessed at) wired into check_stub_behind_stamp.py's walk. One pre-existing false-positive surfaced by the new visibility (hpet_available() returning a real hardware-detection flag, previously invisible because its header ref never resolved) was marked with the existing INTENTIONAL-STUB convention, not suppressed by weakening the resolver.
why: Check 7 can only inspect a stamped symbol it can RESOLVE; an unresolved ref yields no finding, so losing resolution is indistinguishable from passing. This number is the floor: a drop is an ERROR (rc 7). Raising it is the point -- when the resolver improves, update this file in the same commit and say what changed. This file is TRACKED state and is now enforced fail-CLOSED (rc 8) when missing or malformed; STUB_LINT_ALLOW_NO_BASELINE=1 is the deliberate, reported bypass.
standing_gap: 1,514 occurrences not resolved, in evidence-shaped buckets that deliberately do NOT claim a cause: unpaired-ref 1122 (a symbol named with no file to look in), calllike-unresolved 35 (down from 89 -- most of the drop is the resolver-coverage work's head-limit and decl-following wins moving refs out of this bucket), no-calllike-token 47 (no call-like token in that file at all), missing-file 246, non-c-suffix 63, path-escape 1. The names describe what was observed, not why: a call site, a prototype and a macro invocation all carry a call-like token while the real definition lives in another file, so a 'resolver gap' vs 'stale bookkeeping' label would be wrong for a large share of both buckets. unpaired-ref and missing-file are BAD-STORED-DATA classes owned by the stored-ref-repair-in-extraction section of the todo-metadata-layer roadmap (build.py), not the resolver.
largest_recoverable_class: ALL 246 missing-file refs are BARE FILENAMES with no directory component (e.g. `boot_desktop.c:boot_run_deferred`), stored verbatim as repo-relative paths that never exist at the repo root. The files themselves do exist -- boot_desktop.c is src/kernel/main/boot_desktop.c. Of 232 unique such refs, 224 have a UNIQUE basename in the tree, 7 are ambiguous and 1 is absent. That is a larger recoverable class than every other open resolver item combined, and it is owned by the stored-ref-repair-in-extraction section of the todo-metadata-layer roadmap, not this one.
